alex: heads-up — experimenting with a 'surgical cutover' pattern for canaries. goal: swap 5% -> 20% -> 100% but allow surgical rollback per-tenant. thoughts?
ben: sounds like staged cutover but with per-tenant isolation/quorum. how do you plan to manage affinity?
maria: ops concern: KV cache invalidation during partial cutover. we can't afford full cold starts for affected tenants.
alex: plan: pre-warm prefix cache via mirror requests + short-lived warm replicas (2x). use an affinity token cookie to pin sessions during the warm window.
sofi: failure mode to watch: proxy flips routing before warmup completes -> 502/latency spike. propose a rollout controller leader election per-cohort and a 'warmup-complete' readiness signal.
jamie: +1 on readiness signal. also need a manual escape hatch — an API we can call to surgically evict a tenant off the canary ('circuit-surgeon'). Ops should be able to target tenant-id or routing-hash.
alex: minimal commands sketch to operate: 
```
rollout start --cohort=c0 --pct=5 --mode=surgical
rollout promote --cohort=c0 --to=20
rollout abort --cohort=c0 --force
```
ben: telemetry requirements: per-tenant p50/p95, error-rate, model-quality regressions, kv-miss-rate, and a warmup-complete event. need automatic rollback rules when thresholds exceeded.
maria: also add a short 'grace-window' (60s) after flip where we buffer a small sync of mirrored requests to finish cache priming. and set TTLs on warmed cache entries.
sofi: agree. i'll prototype a controller proto that coordinates: leader election -> warmup mirror -> readiness signal -> promote. will include backoff and quiesce logic.
alex: also: routing semantics — keep a dual-path for a tenant during progressive promote (canary + fallback) rather than hard-switch until cutover reaches 100%. reduces blast radius.
jamie: manual UI for 'circuit-surgeon' should show why tenant evicted (metric spikes + recent deploy id) and allow annotated notes. tie into deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: annotated rollout 1718765432, cohort=c0, mode=surgical :white_check_mark:
alex: thanks all. sync tomorrow 11:00 to review prototype and runbook.
